decls.name: SplitsCompletelyRat

paper_span.quote: For a rational prime \(q\), complete splitting in \(L\) means

decls.rationale: `SplitsCompletelyRat q L` formalizes complete splitting of a rational prime: exactly `[L:ℚ]` primes of `𝒪 L` over `(q)`, each with ramification index 1 and residue degree 1 — i.e. \(q\mathcal{O}_L = \mathfrak{p}_1\cdots\mathfrak{p}_{[L:\mathbb{Q}]}\) with residue fields \(\mathbb{F}_q\).

decls.name: SplitsCompletely

paper_span.quote: and it splits completely if there are \([M:F]\) primes above it, all unramified and with

decls.rationale: `SplitsCompletely p` (for `M/F`) is the paper's relative notion: exactly `[M:F]` primes above `p`, each with ramification index 1 and residue degree 1.

decls.name: UnramifiedAtFinitePrimes

paper_span.quote: the exponent \(e(\mathfrak P/\mathfrak p)\) is the ramification index. The prime \(\mathfrak p\) is unramified if all these indices

decls.rationale: `UnramifiedAtFinitePrimes F M` formalizes "unramified at all finite primes": every prime `P` of `𝒪 M` over every prime `p` of `𝒪 F` has ramification index \(e(\mathfrak{P}/\mathfrak{p}) = 1\).

decls.name: EverywhereUnramified

paper_span.quote: unramified'' means unramified at all finite and infinite places.
paper_span.pdf_match: means unramiﬁed at all ﬁnite and inﬁnite places.

decls.rationale: `EverywhereUnramified F M` is the paper's "everywhere unramified": unramified at all finite primes and at all infinite places (no real place of `F` becomes complex in `M`).
